court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: District Judge, Family Court, Kanyakumari Division at Nagercoil (H.M.O.P.No.140 of 2015)
facts_of_case: Wife seeks to set aside exparte decree of divorce granted to husband; husband remarried after statutory period for setting aside the decree

legal_principles.principle: When a marriage has been dissolved by a decree of divorce and either there is no right of appeal against the decree or, if there is such a right of appeal, the time for appealing has expired without an appeal having been presented, or an appeal has been presented but has been dismissed, it shall be lawful for either party to the marriage to marry again.
legal_principles.held: As per Section 15 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, it shall be lawful for either party to re-marry, if no appeal has been filed within a statutory period.
cited_cases: Krishnaveni Rai v. Pankaj Rai and Signature Not Verified Digitally Signed ASWAL Signing Date:21.04.2023 14:58:35 N.C. No. 2023:DHC:2686-DB Anr., (2020) 11 SCC 253
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — applies to all divorce cases

legal_principles.principle: The protection afforded by Section 15 is primarily to a person contesting the decree of divorce.
legal_principles.held: The object of Section 15 is to provide protection to the person who had filed an appeal against the decree of dissolution of marriage and to ensure that such appeal was not frustrated.
cited_cases: Anurag Mittal v. Shaily Mishra Mittal, (2018) 9 SCC 691 : (2018) 4 SCC (Civ) 550
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — highlights the purpose of Section 15

outcome.final_order: Court sets aside exparte decree and allows wife's application to set it aside
